scope: Proposition 9.1 (A finite tidal observation) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 96. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let d ∈ Uϵ, and let w ∈ TΣ be a seed whose future unit timelike geodesic has a noncorner branch as its first runout from the comparison development Pd. Suppose its curvature is bounded in the parallel positive metric up to that runout. For every integer m ≥ 10, every η > 0, and every J > 0, there are smooth complete vacuum data dT ∈ D and seeds wT → w, for arbitrarily large finite T, such that pm(dT − d) −→ 0, and the unit geodesic of wT in the full MGHD of dT has a finite point with tangent UT and a unit spacelike vector XT ⊥ UT for which | |Riem(gdT )(UT , XT , UT , XT ) | | > J. In particular pm(dT − d) < η for sufficiently large T, and the data may be required to remain in any prescribed relatively open neighborhood of d.
